title: A Blood Glucose Control Framework Based on Reinforcement Learning With Safety and Interpretability: In Silico Validation
domain: Type 1 diabetes; automated blood-glucose control in silico.
dataset_or_cohort: UVA/Padova Type 1 Diabetes Simulator v3.2 virtual adult and adolescent populations.
sample_scale: 20 virtual subjects (10 adults and 10 adolescents), each simulated for 20 days.
institution_count: NA — FDA-accepted in-silico simulator rather than a clinical institution cohort.
split_strategy: Online prediction models use the most recent 250 minutes; no independent subject-level train/test split for the control experiment was reported.
observation_process: Glucose, delivered insulin, and meal intake sampled every 5 minutes in simulation; randomized meals and timing.
missingness: NA — complete simulator-generated observations; missingness was not modeled.
censoring_or_competing_events: NA — fixed-duration simulated episodes; no dropout, death, or competing events.
state: Observed glucose, delivered pump insulin, meal intake, and a 9-dimensional DAN context representation used by the controller.
observation_decoder: DAN or random-forest regression predicts future glucose; the simulator supplies subsequent glucose observations.
action: Insulin delivery; the safety actor may suspend/add insulin or recommend oral carbohydrate.
action_provenance: Model-selected simulated pump commands and simulated safety interventions; not clinical orders or administrations.
transition_mechanism: Online data-driven glucose predictor embedded in soft actor-critic control, with short imagined trajectories and a rule-based safety actor.
maximum_horizon: 30-minute glucose prediction, 45-minute safety look-ahead, and 150-minute imagined rollout; closed-loop evaluation lasts 20 days.
rollout_regime: Free-running imagined rollout inside the controller and closed-loop operation in the UVA/Padova simulator.
capability_claim: Planning — sequential insulin control optimized through model rollouts with an explicit safety layer.
baselines: PID controller; DAN versus random-forest glucose prediction. No action-agnostic or shuffled-action model comparator was reported.
state_fidelity_metrics: 30-minute glucose-prediction MAE for DAN and random forest; clinically meaningful control summarized by glucose ranges and CVGA zones.
transition_metrics: One fixed 30-minute prediction horizon; no multi-horizon transition-error profile.
rollout_stability: 20-day closed-loop glucose-control outcomes and safety-actor activation rates; no direct drift/divergence metric for the 150-minute learned rollout.
action_sensitivity: No removal, shuffle, dose-response, or timing sensitivity test of the learned insulin action was reported.
calibration_and_uncertainty: No reliability, interval-coverage, or predictive-calibration evaluation; DAN/RFR point-error comparison only.
external_validation: None; all evaluation used virtual subjects from one simulator version.
decision_utility: Closed-loop simulated glucose control versus PID, including time in target ranges and CVGA outcomes.
safety_evaluation: Explicit hypoglycemia/hyperglycemia look-ahead, insulin/carbohydrate overrides, CVGA safety zones, and safety-actor intervention frequencies.
statistical_analysis: Mean and standard deviation reported; significance testing was reported for selected safety-actor activations, but confidence intervals and resampling details were not reported.
causal_language: Control and safety language; no identified clinical treatment-effect claim.
estimand: NA — sequential simulated control utility, not a causal treatment-effect estimand.
confounding_strategy: NA — randomized simulator scenario rather than observational treatment assignment.
positivity_and_overlap: NA — no observational action-overlap analysis; simulator action support was not formally assessed.
counterfactual_validation: Domain-constrained in-silico control only; no randomized clinical or quasi-experimental validation.
code_access: Unavailable — no inspectable implementation link was reported in the paper.
weights_access: Unavailable — trained predictor/controller parameters were not released.
data_access: Unavailable as a released study dataset; trajectories were generated in the licensed UVA/Padova simulator.
preprocessing_reproducibility: Partial — sampling interval, history length, architecture, rewards, and algorithms are described, but no executable pipeline is provided.
randomness: Meal timing and amount were randomized; seeds and repeated independent training runs were not reported.
evidence_anchors: Methods Sec. III, Figs. 1–2 and Algorithms 1–3 (state, DAN, SAC, safety actor); Experiments Sec. IV-A/B, Table 1 and Figs. 3–4 (prediction/control); Sec. IV-C, Table 2 (safety); Appendix A (parameters).
appraisal_strengths: Long-duration closed-loop evaluation on adult and adolescent virtual subjects with clinically interpretable glycemic and safety outcomes.
appraisal_limitations: Single simulator, no external or real-patient validation, no calibration, no action-ablation test, and no released code/data/weights.

title: A data-driven Alzheimer's disease progression simulator for retrospective validation and prospective Phase III power design.
publication_status: Preprint (medRxiv, 2026; not peer reviewed at inspection cutoff).
domain: Alzheimer disease progression and Phase III clinical-trial simulation.
dataset_or_cohort: ADNI amyloid-positive longitudinal cohort plus published aggregate results from six anti-amyloid randomized trials.
sample_scale: 351 ADNI participants with 1,256 visits; trial simulations used 50–800 participants per arm and 500 repetitions per design.
institution_count: ADNI is multicenter; six external multicenter RCTs. Exact institution count was not reported in the inspected preprint.
split_strategy: Model trained on ADNI; leave-one-trial-out calibration of effect, placebo decline, and variability for trial emulation, while target-trial outcome data were withheld from the stated prospective calculation.
observation_process: Irregular longitudinal amyloid PET, tau PET, MRI atrophy, and clinical measures; simulated trial visits every 3 months.
missingness: Incomplete observations are masked/excluded from the likelihood; complete baseline multimodal records were required for the selected ADNI cohort.
censoring_or_competing_events: Dropout, death, ARIA, and competing events were not modeled in the simulated trials.
state: Latent disease state learned from amyloid, tau, MRI-derived atrophy, and clinical modalities, with trial-specific baseline latent initialization.
observation_decoder: VAE decoders map latent trajectories to multimodal biomarkers and clinical outcomes.
action: Anti-amyloid intervention represented as a piecewise modification of amyloid-clearance dynamics; placebo is the no-intervention comparator.
action_provenance: Simulated treatment profiles calibrated to published aggregate amyloid reductions from six RCTs.
transition_mechanism: Masked amyloid-cascade neural ODE in latent space with VAE observation models.
maximum_horizon: 18- and 27-month Phase III simulations with 3-month visits.
rollout_regime: Free-running latent ODE trajectories for placebo and treated arms, repeated 500 times per trial design.
capability_claim: Counterfactual — compares simulated placebo and alternative anti-amyloid interventions and estimates treatment effects/power.
baselines: Raw SimulAD, ridge regression, and gradient-boosting trial simulators; placebo/no-intervention arm is an action-agnostic comparator.
state_fidelity_metrics: Multimodal reconstruction/trajectory comparisons and aggregate clinical endpoint agreement with published trials; exact metrics vary by modality and trial.
transition_metrics: Longitudinal trajectories and treatment-effect estimates at repeated visits through 18 or 27 months.
rollout_stability: Repeated trial simulations and power curves across sample sizes; no explicit dynamical constraint-violation metric.
action_sensitivity: Six drug-specific clearance profiles and alternative treatment scenarios; treatment magnitude/timing are explicitly encoded, though calibrated from target-drug aggregate data.
calibration_and_uncertainty: Repeated simulations, standard deviations, confidence/prediction intervals, and leave-one-trial-out calibration; no formal predictive reliability or coverage-calibration analysis.
external_validation: Aggregate retrospective comparison with six RCTs; not fully frozen because baseline state and amyloid kinetics are trial-specific and calibrated to published trial information.
decision_utility: Prospective power and sample-size design for Phase III trials, compared with statistical and machine-learning simulators.
safety_evaluation: No adverse-event or ARIA simulation; safety endpoints were outside the model.
statistical_analysis: Linear mixed models for treatment effects, empirical power over 500 repetitions, uncertainty intervals, and leave-one-trial-out analyses.
causal_language: Prospective treatment-effect and placebo-versus-treatment simulation language.
estimand: Between-arm longitudinal treatment effect on clinical outcomes and associated Phase III power.
confounding_strategy: RCT aggregate targets reduce observational confounding for validation, but the simulator itself does not state a full identification strategy.
positivity_and_overlap: Not evaluated; simulated interventions are parameterized from six observed trial profiles rather than assessed for latent-state support.
counterfactual_validation: Retrospective validation against published randomized-trial aggregate outcomes with leave-one-trial-out components; adaptation prevents a fully frozen test.
code_access: Partial/public — training code is inspectable at the paper-reported Inria GitLab; trial-simulation code is stated as planned upon acceptance.
data_access: Credentialed — ADNI data require application; published RCT aggregates are publicly reported.
preprocessing_reproducibility: Partial — cohort criteria, modalities, equations, and pseudocode are detailed, but the full trial pipeline and fitted parameters are not yet released.
randomness: 500 trial repetitions per design; random sampling is described, but reproducible seeds were not reported.
evidence_anchors: Abstract; Methods pp. 6–16 (ADNI cohort, VAE/ODE, interventions, Algorithm 1, trial calibration); Results pp. 17–27 and trial figures/tables (six RCTs, power); Code/data statements near Discussion/Supplement.
appraisal_strengths: Large longitudinal multimodal cohort, explicit intervention operator, repeated Phase III simulations, multiple trial targets, and decision-focused power analysis.
appraisal_limitations: Preprint; trial-specific adaptation, no full causal identification or support analysis, no safety modeling, and incomplete release of trial code/weights.

title: Autosomal Dominant Tubulointerstitial Kidney Disease Clinical Trial Simulator: Case Reports of Model-Informed Drug Development.
publication_status: Peer-reviewed journal article (CPT: Pharmacometrics & Systems Pharmacology, 2026).
domain: Autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease clinical-trial simulation.
dataset_or_cohort: Wake Forest Rare Inherited Kidney Disease Registry: ADTKD-UMOD and ADTKD-MUC1 natural-history cohorts.
sample_scale: 371 UMOD and 233 MUC1 individuals (604 total); high-risk subsets were expanded to synthetic populations of 133 or 150, with simulated trials of 50–200 participants per arm and 100 replicates.
institution_count: One registry/lead institution; geographic recruitment breadth was not quantified in the article.
split_strategy: No new random split reported in this case-study paper; underlying natural-history models reference prior development/test evaluation. Trial scenarios resample synthetic populations.
observation_process: Irregular longitudinal eGFR over years with genotype and demographic covariates; simulated quarterly trial measurements for 1–3 years.
missingness: Missing-data handling for registry trajectories was not reported in sufficient detail in this article.
censoring_or_competing_events: Kidney failure and dropout/censoring were not explicitly modeled in the presented trial cases.
state: Age, baseline eGFR, genotype/SNP features, and individual nonlinear mixed-effects trajectory parameters.
observation_decoder: Parametric nonlinear mixed-effects model generates eGFR trajectories.
action: Hypothetical treatment changes to DPT50, gamma1, or gamma2 disease-progression parameters versus placebo.
action_provenance: User-defined simulated treatment effects, not effects estimated from an administered drug.
transition_mechanism: Sigmoid Imax nonlinear mixed-effects natural-history model fitted with SAEM, including interindividual and residual variability.
maximum_horizon: Quarterly trajectories and trial endpoints over 1, 2, and 3 years.
rollout_regime: Free-running parametric trajectories for placebo and hypothetical treatment arms; 100 replicated trials per scenario.
capability_claim: Counterfactual — simulated placebo-versus-treatment trial outcomes under alternative parameter interventions.
baselines: Placebo/no-change trajectory; alternative effect magnitudes, sample sizes, and study durations. No independent mechanistic model baseline.
state_fidelity_metrics: Real-versus-synthetic marginal distributions and correlations; underlying model VPC/test evidence is referenced to prior work rather than fully re-reported.
transition_metrics: Trial power and endpoint behavior at 1-, 2-, and 3-year durations; no direct horizon-specific trajectory error in this article.
rollout_stability: Power distributions across 100 repetitions and sample sizes; no drift or physiological constraint metric.
action_sensitivity: Defined perturbations of three progression parameters over alternative percentage effects and durations.
calibration_and_uncertainty: Interindividual/residual variability, 100 trial repetitions, and reported confidence intervals; no calibration/coverage audit.
external_validation: No independent institution or geographic cohort validation reported in this article.
decision_utility: Clinical-trial sample-size, duration, endpoint, and enrichment exploration through a public web simulator.
safety_evaluation: No treatment toxicity or clinical safety endpoint was simulated.
statistical_analysis: Power calculations across 100 simulated trials with confidence intervals and scenario comparisons.
causal_language: Hypothetical placebo and treatment-effect simulation; authors caution that the tool does not substitute for clinical evidence.
estimand: Simulated between-arm endpoint difference and probability of detecting a user-specified hypothetical treatment effect.
confounding_strategy: NA — treatment effects are imposed in randomized simulated arms rather than estimated from observational exposure.
positivity_and_overlap: Not evaluated; parameter perturbations are assumed and their empirical treatment support is unknown.
counterfactual_validation: No real treatment-response validation; domain plausibility and prior natural-history model checks only.
code_access: Partial/public — web application and key R examples are available in the article supplement; a complete source repository was not identified.
weights_access: NA — parametric mixed-effects coefficients rather than neural weights; full fitted parameter accessibility is partial.
data_access: Private/governed registry data; synthetic examples are generated by the tool.
preprocessing_reproducibility: Partial — model form and simulation workflow are detailed, but registry preprocessing and complete source pipeline are unavailable.
randomness: 100 replicated simulated trials; random seed was not reported.
evidence_anchors: Methods and model overview, Fig. 1; case studies and Tables/Figs. 2–5 (population synthesis and 1–3-year power); Discussion/Data S1 (web tool and R examples).
appraisal_strengths: Disease-specific natural-history model, explicit trial-design scenarios, repeated power simulations, and an accessible interactive tool.
appraisal_limitations: Hypothetical unvalidated treatment effects, one registry, incomplete missing/censoring reporting, no safety outcomes, and restricted source data.

title: Control of Magnetic Surgical Robots With Model-Based Simulators and Reinforcement Learning.
publication_status: Peer-reviewed journal article (IEEE Transactions on Medical Robotics and Bionics, 2022).
domain: Magnetic surgical robotics and model-based reinforcement learning.
dataset_or_cohort: Physical MagnetoSuture benchtop platform with a 22-gauge needle, four electromagnetic coils, and camera tracking.
sample_scale: 34,742 physical transitions collected in approximately 3.2 hours; downstream simulated training up to 2.5 million steps.
split_strategy: Held-out validation and test transition sets are reported, but exact proportions and leakage controls are not specified.
observation_process: Camera-derived planar needle position and heading after discrete current pulses (100 ms actuation plus 200 ms rest, approximately 3 Hz).
missingness: NA — complete benchtop tracking transitions after data collection/quality filtering; missingness was not modeled.
censoring_or_competing_events: NA — task episodes terminate/reset for target success or leaving the Petri-dish workspace.
observation_decoder: Fully connected neural simulator predicts next needle state.
action_provenance: Manual exploration commands for data collection; learned TD3 commands for simulated training and physical deployment.
transition_mechanism: Deterministic neural one-step model used as a model-based simulator for TD3 policy learning.
maximum_horizon: One-step model validation; policies trained for 500,000–2.5 million simulator steps and evaluated over multi-step physical navigation tasks.
rollout_regime: Free-running simulator during policy training and real closed-loop transfer to the physical device.
capability_claim: Planning — policy selects sequential coil commands using learned-model rollouts.
baselines: Physics-based simulator, pure simulation training, and offline model-free RL variants; no action-agnostic learned-transition comparator.
state_fidelity_metrics: Normalized L2 next-state error (validation 0.033, test 0.045) and physical trajectory RMS error (about 5.3–7.4 mm for learned simulator versus 31 mm physics simulator).
transition_metrics: One-step held-out transition error; no error-versus-rollout-horizon curve.
rollout_stability: Physical center, random-target, and square-path trajectories; no explicit learned-simulator drift/constraint-violation rate by horizon.
action_sensitivity: No action removal, shuffle, or magnitude/timing sensitivity test of the transition model.
calibration_and_uncertainty: No predictive uncertainty or calibration analysis for the deterministic simulator.
external_validation: Simulation-to-real transfer on the same physical apparatus used to collect transitions; useful proxy but not a frozen new device/site.
decision_utility: Real closed-loop needle navigation and trajectory tracking against simulator/control baselines.
safety_evaluation: Reports coil overheating, active cooling, workspace dead zones, out-of-dish termination/reset, and human supervision; no tissue or patient safety test.
statistical_analysis: Point errors and trajectory summaries; repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, and significance tests were not reported.
causal_language: Control/planning language only; no clinical causal-treatment claim.
estimand: NA — embodied task-control utility rather than a causal estimand.
positivity_and_overlap: No formal action-support/coverage analysis for learned policy commands.
counterfactual_validation: NA — no treatment counterfactual claim; validation is simulator-to-real control transfer.
code_access: Unavailable — no inspectable implementation link reported.
weights_access: Unavailable — trained simulator and policy weights were not released.
data_access: Unavailable — collected transition dataset was not released.
preprocessing_reproducibility: Partial — hardware, state extraction, normalization, architecture, and training are described, but executable preprocessing is absent.
randomness: Manual guided exploration and random targets are described; seeds and repeated independent training runs were not reported.
evidence_anchors: Methods Sec. IV-B.1–5 (hardware, data, simulator, TD3); Experiments Sec. V-A–D, Tables I–II and Figs. 4–6 (errors and physical tasks); Conclusion Sec. VI.
appraisal_strengths: Direct physical data collection and real closed-loop transfer with comparison to a physics simulator and alternative training regimes.
appraisal_limitations: Single apparatus, one-step simulator metric only, no uncertainty/action ablation, limited safety scope, and no public artifacts.

title: Development of a model-based clinical trial simulation platform to optimize the design of clinical trials for Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
publication_status: Peer-reviewed journal article (CPT: Pharmacometrics & Systems Pharmacology, 2022).
domain: Duchenne muscular dystrophy disease-progression and clinical-trial simulation.
dataset_or_cohort: Duchenne Regulatory Science Consortium database: 15 clinical studies comprising trials and natural-history cohorts.
sample_scale: 1,505 participants and 27,252 observations; development: 11 North American studies (1,141 participants, 19,996 observations); external: four non-US studies (364 participants, 7,256 observations).
institution_count: Multicenter across 15 studies; exact site count was not reported.
split_strategy: Geographic/study split: 11 North American development studies and four non-US external validation studies.
observation_process: Irregular longitudinal clinical outcomes from age 4 through advanced disease: NSAA, FVC, and climb/stand/walk-run velocities.
missingness: No imputation of missing dependent variables or covariates; missing categorical covariates grouped where applicable.
censoring_or_competing_events: Inability to perform functional tests due to severity is likelihood-censored (M4); dropout is not modeled and is acknowledged as a limitation.
state: Age, baseline functional score, race, steroid use, mutation class, study type, and individual random effects.
observation_decoder: Nonlinear mixed-effects trajectories for five clinical endpoints.
action: User-defined hypothetical treatment timing and magnitude applied to progression-model parameters to create active arms.
action_provenance: Simulated treatment effects; not estimated from observed treatment response in the platform evaluation.
transition_mechanism: Product of Chapman–Richards growth and sigmoid Imax decline functions with fixed/random effects and residual error.
maximum_horizon: Age-spanning natural-history trajectories and user-defined trial durations; external VPCs cover observed longitudinal follow-up.
rollout_regime: Free-running parametric trajectory simulation, virtual trials, and visual predictive checks with 500 simulated datasets.
capability_claim: Counterfactual — placebo/historical-control versus hypothetical active treatment trial simulation.
baselines: Observed development and external cohorts; placebo/historical-control trajectory versus active-arm parameter shifts.
state_fidelity_metrics: Goodness-of-fit plots and visual predictive checks for five endpoints with observed percentiles versus simulated prediction intervals.
transition_metrics: Age-resolved longitudinal VPCs in development and external cohorts; no single aggregate transition metric.
rollout_stability: VPC trajectory envelopes and trial simulations; dropout and some long-term endpoint transitions remain unmodeled.
action_sensitivity: Treatment-effect size, timing, and affected parameter can be varied in the CTS platform.
calibration_and_uncertainty: Interindividual/residual variability, 500-simulation VPC intervals, 1,000 bootstraps, and 90% confidence intervals; no explicit coverage-calibration statistic.
external_validation: Frozen evaluation on four non-US studies held out from model development.
decision_utility: Trial-design platform for endpoint, enrichment, duration, placebo/historical-control, and treatment-effect scenarios; no prospective decision-impact study.
safety_evaluation: No adverse-event, toxicity, or harmful-decision evaluation.
statistical_analysis: NONMEM estimation, 1,000 bootstrap replicates, 500 VPC simulations, confidence intervals, and covariate modeling.
causal_language: Hypothetical treatment-effect and historical-control simulation language.
estimand: Simulated active-versus-control endpoint contrast under a user-specified treatment effect.
confounding_strategy: NA for randomized virtual arms; historical-control use is proposed without a complete real-world confounding strategy.
positivity_and_overlap: Not evaluated for hypothetical interventions or historical-control transport.
counterfactual_validation: No observed treatment-effect validation; natural-history dynamics receive frozen geographic external validation.
code_access: Public/partial — NONMEM model codes are provided in the article supplement.
weights_access: NA — parametric NONMEM coefficients rather than neural weights; parameter estimates are reported/supplemented.
data_access: Governed consortium data; not openly downloadable.
preprocessing_reproducibility: Partial — CDISC harmonization, endpoint definitions, model equations, and code are described, but source data are restricted.
randomness: 500 simulated VPC datasets and 1,000 bootstraps; seeds were not reported.
evidence_anchors: Methods (database, endpoint models, censoring, geographic split); Tables 1–3; Figs. 1–5 and external VPC supplement; Discussion and Appendix S5 (model code).
appraisal_strengths: Large multisource longitudinal dataset, prespecified geographic external set, five endpoints, explicit censoring model, and public model code.
appraisal_limitations: Treatment effects are hypothetical, dropout and safety are not modeled, governed data limit reproduction, and clinical decision impact is untested.

title: Generating whole-brain neural activity and behavior through unified latent dynamics
publication_status: Preprint (bioRxiv/openRxiv version 2, 2026; not peer reviewed at inspection cutoff).
domain: Whole-brain neural dynamics and behavior in C. elegans.
dataset_or_cohort: Public Kato et al. whole-brain calcium-imaging recording of an immobilized wild-type C. elegans.
sample_scale: One approximately 1,080-second recording with 109 neurons and seven fictive behavioral states; autonomous rollouts up to 30,000 steps.
split_strategy: No independent train/test recording; model fit and generative comparisons use the same recorded session.
observation_process: Whole-brain calcium activity and manually/algorithmically assigned fictive behavior sampled as a continuous time series; downstream body motion is heuristic/simulated.
missingness: Missing-neuron or observation handling was not reported; analysis uses the selected recorded traces.
censoring_or_competing_events: NA — one fixed experimental recording; no clinical censoring or competing events.
state: Three-dimensional latent state inferred from neural causal history.
observation_decoder: RNN decoders generate 109-neuron activity and discrete behavior; behavior is mapped heuristically to eigenworms/ElegansBot motion.
action: Latent noise injection and state-steering intervention; no observed biological action or treatment variable in the base model.
action_provenance: Purely simulated latent interventions selected by investigators.
transition_mechanism: Stochastic Gaussian Markov transition in latent space with neural and behavioral recurrent decoders.
maximum_horizon: 30,000-step autonomous rollout (reported as approximately 168 minutes); robustness/steering experiments include 60-second and 10,000-step simulations.
rollout_regime: Autonomous free-running stochastic latent dynamics with repeated generated trajectories and simulated steering.
capability_claim: Counterfactual — paper explicitly presents latent interventions/steering as counterfactual manipulation of neural-behavior dynamics.
baselines: Recorded-session statistics and unsteered generated trajectories; no independent learned action-agnostic model.
state_fidelity_metrics: Neural functional-connectivity agreement (reported R²), behavior occupancy/frequency divergence, and decoded behavior/state structure.
transition_metrics: Behavior transition-matrix correlations/divergences and generated trajectory statistics; evaluated on same-session distributions.
rollout_stability: 30,000-step generation, 1,000 rollouts to 60 seconds, and robustness across intervention-noise intensities.
action_sensitivity: Unsteered baseline versus latent noise/desired-state steering at varied intensities; interventions are not validated against biological perturbations.
calibration_and_uncertainty: Stochastic variance and repeated rollouts are reported; no predictive calibration or interval coverage.
external_validation: None; no second worm, session, strain, or laboratory dataset.
decision_utility: Simulated goal-directed steering and body-motion visualization only; no real biological or clinical decision evaluation.
safety_evaluation: NA for the demonstrated nonclinical in-silico neural model; no hazard evaluation.
statistical_analysis: KL divergences, chi-square tests, correlations/R², repeated stochastic simulations, and selected p-values.
causal_language: Explicit counterfactual intervention and control language for latent dynamics.
estimand: No explicit biological intervention-effect estimand; outcomes are model-generated state/behavior trajectories.
confounding_strategy: None; observational neural sequence plus simulated intervention.
positivity_and_overlap: Not evaluated; latent interventions have no empirical action-support analysis.
counterfactual_validation: No real perturbation experiment; only internal model/domain consistency.
code_access: Unavailable — no inspectable implementation link identified in the preprint.
weights_access: Unavailable — fitted model weights were not released.
data_access: Public — source neural/behavior recording is linked through the cited OSF dataset.
preprocessing_reproducibility: Partial — architecture and transformation steps are described, but code, exact pipeline, and fitted parameters are unavailable.
randomness: Large repeated stochastic rollout sets are reported; exact reproducible seeds were not reported.
evidence_anchors: Results Secs. 2.2–2.5, Figs. 2–4 (generation, transitions, interventions); Discussion Sec. 3; Methods Secs. 4.1–4.5 (dataset, latent model, decoding); Fig. S1.
appraisal_strengths: Long autonomous stochastic rollouts, joint neural/behavior decoding, multiple fidelity statistics, and explicit intervention demonstrations.
appraisal_limitations: Single training/evaluation recording, no held-out subject/session, no biological perturbation validation, no calibration, and no code/weights.

title: Machine Learning for Mechanical Ventilation Control
publication_status: Preprint (medRxiv/arXiv version 4, 2021; not peer reviewed in inspected source).
domain: Mechanical ventilation control on a physical test lung.
dataset_or_cohort: Open-source PVP ventilator connected to a commercial QuickLung test lung across six resistance/compliance settings.
sample_scale: Ten ventilators, four compressors, and two control servers are described; exact number of simulator-training breaths/transitions was not reported. PID benchmark used 2,400 trajectories per lung setting.
split_strategy: Random 20% held-out open-loop sequences for simulator testing; controller evaluation uses physical closed-loop trials across six lung settings and target waveforms.
observation_process: High-frequency airway pressure and valve-control histories during approximately 9-second, 300-step breaths; six R/C lung settings.
missingness: NA — controlled benchtop sensor streams; missingness was not modeled.
censoring_or_competing_events: NA — fixed breath/control episodes with explicit abort/reset conditions.
state: Recent pressure history and control history, with lung resistance/compliance setting implicit through separate models.
observation_decoder: Deep dynamics model predicts next airway pressure.
action: Continuous inspiratory valve command; expiratory control is hard-coded.
action_provenance: Safe PI/PID-guided physical exploration commands and learned controller commands deployed on hardware.
transition_mechanism: Autoregressive neural pressure simulator; PID-residual neural controller and RL baselines trained using model rollouts.
maximum_horizon: Open-loop simulator error evaluated across 25 recursive steps; closed-loop breath control spans 300 steps (about 9 seconds/three breaths).
rollout_regime: Recursive free-running pressure simulation and real closed-loop hardware control.
capability_claim: Planning — learned controller selects sequential inspiratory actions using a learned simulator.
baselines: P, PI, PID, PPO, DQN, model-free/model-based controller variants; no action-agnostic transition comparator.
state_fidelity_metrics: Pressure MAE across six R/C settings (approximately 0.39–0.85 in reported units) and physical waveform L1 tracking error.
transition_metrics: Open-loop error plotted by recursive prediction step to 25 steps (Fig. 5).
rollout_stability: Closed-loop pressure tracking over full breaths and multiple target waveforms/settings; hardware safety aborts constrain failures.
action_sensitivity: Safe exploratory valve commands use boundary and triangular perturbations; no shuffled/removal action-model ablation.
calibration_and_uncertainty: No predictive uncertainty or formal calibration reported.
external_validation: Simulator-to-real controller transfer across six test-lung settings on the same hardware family; no new site/device population.
decision_utility: Real closed-loop pressure-control performance versus PID and RL/controller baselines.
safety_evaluation: Software pressure/volume/disconnection/delay checks, hard-coded expiratory control, and a mechanical safety valve with abort behavior.
statistical_analysis: Point/aggregate errors and benchmark comparisons; confidence intervals and inferential tests were not reported.
causal_language: Control/planning language only; no clinical treatment-effect claim.
estimand: NA — physical control performance rather than a causal estimand.
positivity_and_overlap: Targeted exploration is constrained around safe baseline controllers, but formal action-overlap/coverage diagnostics are not reported.
counterfactual_validation: NA — no treatment counterfactual claim; evaluation is simulator-to-real control transfer.
code_access: Unavailable for the reported learned simulator/controller; the underlying PVP ventilator platform is open source.
weights_access: Unavailable — learned model/controller weights were not released.
data_access: Unavailable — collected pressure/control trajectories were not released.
preprocessing_reproducibility: Partial — hardware, signals, history windows, architectures, and training procedures are described; exact data volume and executable pipeline are absent.
randomness: Random targeted exploration is described; seeds and repeated independent training runs were not reported.
evidence_anchors: Methods pp. 5–8, Secs. 3–5 and Figs. 3–9 (system, exploration, simulator, control); Sec. 4.1/Fig. 5 (25-step error); Appendix B pp. 13–15, Tables 3–5.
appraisal_strengths: Physical closed-loop validation, multiple lung mechanics and waveform targets, horizon-resolved simulator error, strong control baselines, and explicit hardware safeguards.
appraisal_limitations: Benchtop rather than patient validation, same-platform transfer, no uncertainty/calibration, incomplete dataset reporting, and no released learned artifacts.

title: OMG-RL:Offline Model-based Guided Reward Learning for Heparin Treatment
publication_status: Peer-reviewed journal article (Biomedical Engineering Advances, 2025); full coding used the publicly accessible arXiv v2 manuscript because the version-of-record PDF was not retrievable without the publisher interface.
domain: EHR-based heparin dosing and offline reinforcement learning.
dataset_or_cohort: MIMIC-III adult ICU records for patients receiving intravenous heparin.
institution_count: One source health system/database (Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center MIMIC-III).
split_strategy: Random 80/20 patient split into training and test sets.
observation_process: Hourly records from 7 to 72 hours after heparin treatment, including laboratory values, vital signs, scores, and outcomes.
missingness: High-missingness variables removed; outliers screened; sample-and-hold plus KNN/linear imputation and normalization applied.
censoring_or_competing_events: Trajectories are truncated to 7–72 hours; death/discharge and informative treatment discontinuation are not modeled as censoring/competing events.
state: Sixteen preprocessed clinical variables excluding aPTT and heparin dose from the state vector.
observation_decoder: Probabilistic ensemble predicts next clinical state and reward.
action: Intravenous heparin dose discretized into six quantile-based action classes.
action_provenance: Observed clinician-administered/recorded doses for offline data; learned policy actions during model rollout.
transition_mechanism: Ensemble probabilistic dynamics model with recursive rollout, conservative model-based Q learning, and guided reward learning.
rollout_regime: Free-running model rollouts for policy training/evaluation plus offline weighted-importance-sampling evaluation on held-out patients.
capability_claim: Planning — optimizes a sequential heparin dosing policy through learned-model rollouts.
baselines: COMBO, SAC, BCQ, Double DQN, Dueling DQN, and DQN in model-free/model-based variants; no action-agnostic transition comparator.
state_fidelity_metrics: No direct next-state clinical prediction metric; model adequacy is inferred from policy returns, Q values, WIS, and treatment-success proxies.
transition_metrics: No one-step or horizon-specific state-transition error reported.
rollout_stability: 36-hour simulated treatment episodes; no model-drift, constraint-violation, or error-versus-horizon analysis.
action_sensitivity: No action removal, shuffle, dose-class perturbation, or support-stratified sensitivity test.
calibration_and_uncertainty: Ensemble variance/conservatism is used as a model-error proxy; no calibration or interval coverage.
external_validation: None; held-out patients come from the same MIMIC-III source.
decision_utility: Offline policy value via WIS and simulated 36-hour therapeutic-success episodes; no prospective or clinician-in-the-loop evaluation.
safety_evaluation: aPTT therapeutic-range reward is a limited safety proxy; bleeding, thrombosis, overdose severity, contraindications, and override/failure tests are not evaluated.
statistical_analysis: Five- or ten-run mean/standard-deviation comparisons, box plots, WIS, and repeated 36-hour treatment-success simulations; confidence intervals and formal significance tests are not reported.
causal_language: Claims improved treatment policy versus clinician/model baselines, but no complete causal identification analysis.
estimand: Offline policy value/return under the learned dosing regime, estimated partly with WIS.
confounding_strategy: No explicit adjustment for time-varying confounding beyond state conditioning and offline RL/OPE.
positivity_and_overlap: No behavior-policy overlap or effective-sample-size diagnostics for WIS; six action bins alone do not establish support.
counterfactual_validation: Offline WIS on held-out MIMIC-III plus learned-model simulation; no randomized, quasi-experimental, or external treatment validation.
code_access: Unavailable — no inspectable implementation repository identified.
weights_access: Unavailable — ensemble/policy weights were not released.
data_access: Credentialed public — MIMIC-III requires data-use training and approval.
preprocessing_reproducibility: Partial — cohort, variables, time window, imputation, action bins, algorithms, and hyperparameters are described, but code is absent.
randomness: Five/ten repeated experiments and random model/initial-state selection are reported; exact seeds are not.
evidence_anchors: Methods pp. 5–7 and Algorithms 1–2 (dynamics/reward/policy); Experimental Setup pp. 7–8, Secs. 5.1–5.2 (MIMIC split/state/action); Results pp. 8–13, Figs. 2–8 (WIS/rollouts); limitations p. 13.
appraisal_strengths: Explicit dose actions, held-out-patient OPE, broad RL baselines, repeated experiments, and clinically interpretable aPTT target.
appraisal_limitations: No direct dynamics fidelity, calibration, support/confounding audit, external validation, comprehensive safety test, or released implementation.

title: SimulAD: a dynamical model for personalized simulation and disease staging in Alzheimer's disease.
domain: Alzheimer disease progression, personalized staging, and simulation.
dataset_or_cohort: ADNI development cohort and independent Geneva Memory Center (GMC) clinical cohort.
sample_scale: 442 ADNI participants and 93 GMC participants; 50 GMC participants had tau PET; GMC follow-up included 201 MMSE assessments across groups.
institution_count: ADNI multicenter development cohort plus one independent Geneva memory-center cohort.
split_strategy: Previously fitted ADNI model applied to GMC; GMC-specific imputation/harmonization and a separately estimated GMC trajectory are also used, so the external analysis is not wholly frozen.
observation_process: Irregular longitudinal clinical scores and MRI/amyloid-PET/FDG-PET in ADNI; GMC has baseline multimodal imaging and longitudinal MMSE only.
missingness: Disease severity can use available modalities; six absent GMC clinical scores are KNN-imputed from ADNI, 36 missing FDG scans are estimated from early amyloid PET, and tracer measurements are harmonized.
censoring_or_competing_events: Conversion status uses last follow-up; dropout, death, and informative follow-up are not modeled.
state: Four biomarker z-scores: clinical, gray-matter atrophy, amyloid, and glucose metabolism; disease severity is position on the reference trajectory.
observation_decoder: Mappings convert z-score trajectories back to clinical and regional imaging measurements, including MMSE.
action: No action evaluated in this study; the paper cites prior capability to simulate anti-amyloid treatment effects.
action_provenance: NA for current experiments; referenced anti-amyloid action is a simulated intervention from prior work.
transition_mechanism: Coupled ordinary differential equations governing the four biomarker z-scores.
maximum_horizon: Personalized GMC evolution simulated for five years; ADNI/GMC reference trajectories span long-term disease time.
rollout_regime: Free-running forward/backward ODE trajectories and five-year individual prediction.
capability_claim: Passive forecasting/disease staging in the present experiments; the paper additionally repeats a counterfactual anti-amyloid capability claim from prior work.
baselines: ADNI-derived versus GMC-derived progression trajectories and known clinical groups; no standard forecasting baseline or action-agnostic intervention model.
state_fidelity_metrics: Known-groups t tests/effect sizes and Spearman correlations with MMSE, hippocampal atrophy, FDG, amyloid, and external tau PET.
transition_metrics: ADNI-versus-GMC trajectory errors (6%–9% for z-scores; 3%–12% for decoded modalities) and GMC MMSE absolute error 1.8–2.4 points over follow-up.
rollout_stability: Five-year illustrative individual trajectories and cohort trajectory comparisons; no error degradation at multiple forecast horizons.
action_sensitivity: No action perturbation experiment in this paper.
calibration_and_uncertainty: Standard deviations and 95% confidence intervals for selected regressions/imputation; no predictive calibration or interval coverage.
external_validation: Independent GMC cohort with different acquisition protocols, but adaptation/harmonization uses GMC data and a GMC-specific progression fit.
decision_utility: Retrospective disease staging and individual MMSE monitoring proxy; no clinician decision or trial-enrollment impact study.
statistical_analysis: Student t tests, Cohen d, Spearman correlations, 10-fold cross-validation for imputation, means/SDs, and 95% confidence intervals.
causal_language: Paper states SimulAD can simulate anti-amyloid treatment impact, but the current empirical evaluation does not estimate or validate such an effect.
estimand: Individual natural-history biomarker/MMSE trajectory; no explicit intervention-effect estimand in the current study.
confounding_strategy: None for the referenced treatment capability; external natural-history validation uses cohort harmonization rather than causal adjustment.
counterfactual_validation: None in the current paper; external GMC validation concerns staging and natural-history trajectories only.
code_access: Unavailable — the article calls SimulAD research software and provides no inspectable repository.
weights_access: Unavailable — fitted ODE/decoder parameters were not released as a reusable package.
data_access: ADNI is credentialed; GMC data availability is request/institution-governed and not openly released.
preprocessing_reproducibility: Partial — imaging pipelines, KNN imputation, FDG estimation, and tracer correction are described, but complete code/data are unavailable.
randomness: No reproducible seeds or repeated stochastic model runs; deterministic ODE analysis with resampling only for imputation validation.
evidence_anchors: pp. 73–76, Secs. 2.1–2.6 and Tables 1–2 (cohorts/model/preprocessing); pp. 78–80, Figs. 3–6 and Table 4 (external validity, trajectory errors, five-year MMSE); pp. 80–82 Discussion/Conclusion.
appraisal_strengths: Independent clinical cohort, multimodal staging checks including tau not used for training, explicit heterogeneity harmonization, and individual longitudinal prediction.
appraisal_limitations: External cohort is adapted rather than fully frozen, no standard forecast baseline or horizon degradation, no calibration/public code, and treatment counterfactual capability is not tested here.

title: The Coupled Stochastic Dynamical System: A Generative Model for Simulating and Forecasting Youth Mental Health Trajectories
publication_status: Preprint (medRxiv, posted July 29, 2026; not peer reviewed at inspection cutoff).
domain: Youth mental health, digital phenotyping, wearable sensing, and mechanistic virtual twins.
dataset_or_cohort: GLOBEM multi-year university-student cohort integrating passive smartphone, wearable, EMA, and survey data.
sample_scale: 496 participants; four empirical clusters; participant-level decoding/forecasting uses the 50 centroid-nearest participants per cluster (200 total).
institution_count: GLOBEM is a longitudinal research cohort; exact collection-site count was not stated in the inspected primary text.
split_strategy: Cluster/participant inversion uses observed summaries; forecasting uses causal rolling origins with future observations withheld. Split-half corridor analysis tests leakage, but there is no independent external cohort.
observation_process: Daily digital/wearable channels and sparser EMA/survey channels on irregular grids; forecasts at 1, 3, 7, 14, and 21 days.
missingness: Observed time points retained; missing channels marginalized when availability thresholds are met, otherwise state labels remain missing. No blanket imputation/deletion solely for missing channels.
censoring_or_competing_events: Observation length is participant-specific; dropout/informative missingness and clinical competing events are not modeled.
state: Multiscale traits, day-level psychiatric burden, sub-hourly behavior/physiology, latent HMM states, and participant-specific compatible parameter clouds.
observation_decoder: Mixed-emission sticky HMM/AR-HMM decodes digital, wearable, and EMA channels and produces channel-specific forecasts.
action: Architecture includes intervention-process namespaces and motivates counterfactual changes, but no intervention action is perturbed in the reported empirical experiments.
action_provenance: NA for evaluated experiments; proposed actions are future simulated behavioral/intervention perturbations.
transition_mechanism: Coupled stochastic processes and oscillators with explicit feedbacks; ABC sequential-rejection inversion; sticky HMM/AR-HMM forecast dynamics.
maximum_horizon: Participant-matched simulator durations; rolling forecasts at 1, 3, 7, 14, and 21 days; cluster inversion uses 80-day simulated populations.
rollout_regime: Free-running stochastic virtual-twin generation and offline rolling-origin forecasts with locked synthetic models.
capability_claim: Counterfactual — title/body position the CSDS for counterfactual simulation and intervention planning, although reported evaluation is passive generation/forecasting.
baselines: Causal prefix mean, persistence, sticky HMM, sticky HMM plus AR heads, native AR-HMM, and synthetic versus hybrid training regimes; no evaluated no-action/action-shuffle counterfactual comparator.
state_fidelity_metrics: Target coverage/proximity; synthetic-observed state occupancy correlation/total-variation distance, transition correlation/Jensen-Shannon divergence, and state-fingerprint correlation.
transition_metrics: Transition-matrix concordance plus pooled predictive R², within-subject skill, directional balanced accuracy, and drift correlation at 1/3/7/14/21 days.
rollout_stability: Repeated simulations per particle/participant, horizon-resolved performance, split-half target-corridor stability, and discussion of horizon-dependent deterioration; no clinical constraint-violation rate.
action_sensitivity: No intervention removal, timing, magnitude, or counterfactual perturbation test; these are explicitly future priorities.
calibration_and_uncertainty: Compatible parameter ensembles, participant uncertainty corridors, 5,000 subject-block bootstrap intervals, and horizon-specific calibration plots/linear fits at 1 and 21 days.
external_validation: None; all empirical fitting and evaluation use GLOBEM, with temporally held-out observations but no independent cohort.
decision_utility: Offline short-horizon risk/trajectory forecasting proxy; no clinician decision, intervention selection, or prospective workflow evaluation.
safety_evaluation: Low-burden structural constraints for unmeasured syndromes and a relaxed suicidality constraint are used, but hazardous-transition calibration and clinical safety testing are explicitly absent.
statistical_analysis: ANOVA with Holm correction, FDR correction, effect sizes, ABC diagnostics, correlations/divergences, and 5,000 subject-block bootstrap confidence intervals.
causal_language: Explicit causal-pathway, counterfactual-simulation, virtual-twin, and intervention-planning language, with Discussion cautioning that recovered parameters are not unique causal determinants.
estimand: No explicit intervention contrast; evaluated quantities are phenotype fit, state concordance, and future observational trajectory prediction.
confounding_strategy: None for intervention effects; forecasts use causal temporal prefixes, but that prevents look-ahead rather than identifying treatment effects.
positivity_and_overlap: Not evaluated because no empirical intervention/action study is conducted.
counterfactual_validation: None; paper calls for future perturbation, prospective, and independent-cohort tests.
code_access: Planned/unavailable — paper states the accepted-manuscript code base will contain the full implementation; no inspectable repository was identified at cutoff.
weights_access: Unavailable — accepted particle clouds/fitted participant models were not released.
data_access: GLOBEM is a released research dataset by citation; data produced in this study are stated available on reasonable request.
preprocessing_reproducibility: Partial — extensive supplementary specifications and mapping/ABC/HMM settings are described, but current code and exact fitted artifacts are unavailable.
randomness: ABC proposal populations, 7–15 simulation repetitions, 20×50 participant simulations, and 5,000 bootstrap resamples; exact seeds not reported.
evidence_anchors: Abstract pp. 2; Methods pp. 5–15, Secs. 2.1–2.7 (architecture, inversion, missingness, forecasts, code); Results pp. 16–20, Tables 3–4 and Figs. 3–5; Discussion pp. 20–25; Data availability p. 26.
appraisal_strengths: Explicit mechanistic architecture, individualized stochastic twins, strong synthetic-to-observed state/transition tests, causal rolling-origin evaluation, horizon-resolved metrics, calibration plots, and block-bootstrap uncertainty.
appraisal_limitations: Preprint; one nonclinical student cohort, target specifications reuse participant summaries, no evaluated intervention despite counterfactual claims, no external/prospective clinical validation, and code/weights unavailable.
